Bug_Details: Optional.of() always returns a non-empty optional. Using ifPresent/isPresent/orElse/orElseGet/orElseThrow/isPresent/or/orNull method on it is unnecessary and most probably a bug.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by using the isPresent() method on an Optional object that is guaranteed to be non-empty due to the use of Optional.of(). This check is redundant and can be considered a bug.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with a non-null input. The showBug method uses isPresent() on an Optional object that is guaranteed to be non-empty due to the use of Optional.of(), which is redundant and can be considered a bug.
